faqs.q: What is the right age to start investing?
faqs.a: There is no fixed right age; the earlier you start, the more years compounding has to work. Many people begin once they have a regular income, have set aside some money for emergencies and understand their goals and how much risk they can handle.

faqs.q: How much money do I need to start investing?
faqs.a: You do not need a large sum. Many mutual funds let you invest small amounts every month through a SIP, so you can begin with whatever you can set aside regularly and increase it as your income grows. Consistency over many years usually matters more than the starting amount.

faqs.q: What is the difference between saving and investing?
faqs.a: Saving means keeping money safe and easy to access, such as in a bank account, usually with low returns. Investing means putting money into assets like stocks, mutual funds or bonds that can grow faster over time but can also fall in value. Most people keep savings for short-term needs and invest for long-term goals.

faqs.q: Is it risky to start investing when you are young?
faqs.a: All market-linked investments carry risk, but starting young gives you more time to ride out market falls and recover. Because younger investors usually have fewer obligations, they can often accept more ups and downs in exchange for higher potential returns, as long as the choice matches their own risk tolerance and goals.
